niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want Jungian self-inquiry, a regular meditation practice, or a broader spiritual path. These are good starting points based on the available course information:

### Shadow work
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A practical, Jungian-oriented option with video and audio lessons and exercises intended for everyday use. A good fit if you want guided self-reflection rather than a clinical training.
- **[Encounters with the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/encounters-with-the-shadow)** — A shorter introduction, with videos, audio, and a companion guide. Consider it if you’d like to sample the topic before committing to a longer course.
- **[Shadow Work: Heal & Integrate Your Shadow Self — Udemy](https://www.udemy.com/course/shadow_work/)** — A self-paced, exercise-based option. Since course quality and instructor background can vary on marketplaces, check the instructor’s qualifications, syllabus, and recent reviews before enrolling.

### Meditation and spiritual practice
- **[Mindfulness Daily — Tara Brach and Jack Kornfield](https://www.tarabrach.com/online-courses/)** — A free, 40-day guided training for building a regular mindfulness practice. A strong choice if you want a structured daily routine.
- **[Mindfulness: What It Is, Where It Comes From, and How to Practice It — Naropa University](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — A free introductory course that connects contemporary mindfulness with Buddhist traditions and offers practices to try.
- **[The Three Turnings of the Wheel — Naropa University](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — A deeper Buddhist contemplative option combining study, meditation, and compassion practice.

**A sensible path:** Start with one introductory shadow-work course and one meditation course, rather than taking several intensive programs at once. Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions; go slowly, pause if you feel overwhelmed, and consider working with a licensed mental-health professional if you’re dealing with trauma or significant distress. These courses can support personal reflection, but they aren’t a substitute for therapy or professional training. Check each provider’s current syllabus, schedule, and price before signing up.
